definitions.explanation: Large in number or amount. The opposite of 少ない (すくない - few). Used for both countable and uncountable things.

examples.japanese: ⟦{宿題|しゅくだい}→宿題：00812_shukudai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{多|おお}い。

examples.english: This book has a lot of text.
There are many people today, aren't there?

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{町|まち}→町：00613_machi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{車|くるま}→車：00516_kuruma⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{多|おお}くて、⟦{道|みち}→道：00505_michi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いつも→いつも：00599_itsumo⟧⟦{混|こ}んでいる→混む：02574_komu⟧。
examples.english: There are many cars in this town, so the roads are always crowded.

examples.japanese: ⟦{最近|さいきん}→最近：00881_saikin⟧、⟦{雨|あめ}→雨：00583_ame⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{日|ひ}→日：02249_hi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{多|おお}い⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧、⟦{洗濯物|せんたくもの}→洗濯物：09533_sentakumono⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{乾|かわ}かない→乾く：00786_kawaku⟧。
examples.english: There have been many rainy days recently, so the laundry won't dry.

notes: {多|おお}い conjugates as an i-adjective: {多|おお}くない (negative), {多|おお}くて (te-form), {多|おお}かった (past). Important: {多|おお}い usually cannot directly modify nouns (× {多|おお}い{人|ひと}). Instead, say {人|ひと}が{多|おお}い or use たくさんの. However, {多|おお}くの (おおくの - many) can modify nouns: {多|おお}くの{人|ひと} (many people).
